transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (Pioneer CTO), Priya Raman (Pioneer Lead ML Eng)

[00:00] Alex Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro \u2014 I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, this is Maya our solutions engineer. how's everyboddy?
[00:08] Daniel Cho: good, thanks. running a bit late this morning but all set.
[00:12] Maya Singh: awesome. we'll keep this to ~30-40, give you a demo of hosted API for chat and text gen basics, and leave time for Qs \u2014 especially on streaming and retries.
[00:22] Priya Raman: great, we're mainly curious about latency and how chunked streaming works for our realtime assistant. also cost implications.
[00:30] Alex Park: perfect. quick qual \u2014 what's your current stack for models and infra? are you running anything in prod today?
[00:36] Daniel Cho: we have an in-house LLM pipeline for inference for analytics summarization, but it's not production-grade for chat. mostly using a third-party API for prototypes \u2014 it's been okay but costs are spiking.
[00:47] Priya Raman: also we need SSO/SAML + audit logs for compliance, and key management with our KMS.
[00:54] Maya Singh: noted. Redwood supports SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations \u2014 we'll share the docs after.
[01:02] Alex Park: quick agenda: 1) Hosted API basics, 2) streaming demo, 3) params & retries, 4) Q&A, and next steps. sound good?
[01:10] Daniel Cho: yep.

--- Demo start ---

[01:14] Maya Singh: I'll share my screen \u2014 demo is using a small chat app hitting Redwood hosted endpoint. Starting with a simple chat stream: you call the /v1/chat/completions endpoint with stream=true and we'll show incremental events.
[01:30] Maya Singh: here you see a single request payload \u2014 model name, messages array, and streaming flag. we also include a request_id for idempotency in our client.
[01:40] Priya Raman: is the request_id required?
[01:42] Maya Singh: not strictly required, but recommended for safe retries \u2014 if a client retries with same request_id within the idempotency window, Redwood can de-dupe or resume in some cases depending on model.
[01:53] Alex Park: also we surface a streaming protocol that emits partial tokens as they generate; client can concat. this reduces time-to-first-token vs waiting for full response.
[02:04] [02:04] Speaker 3: mm-hmm
[02:08] Maya Singh: note \u2014 streaming doesn't change pricing; you still pay per token generated. but it helps perceived latency for the user.
[02:18] Daniel Cho: what's typical latency to first token?
[02:20] Maya Singh: depends on model and context length \u2014 for our curated small LMs it's often 50-120ms to first token on hosted region; larger models higher. for guaranteed p95 you'd look at Dedicated.
[02:34] Priya Raman: can you demo network errors and retry behavior? that's our big concern.
[02:39] Maya Singh: sure \u2014 two patterns: client-side retry with idempotency key, and server-driven progress tokens. in demo I'll simulate a dropped connection.
[02:49] [03:00] Maya Singh: (simulates) connection drop \u2014 client receives partial stream + an error. if it has request_id it can retry; Redwood will reconcile if generation was completed. otherwise client may get duplicated content, so dedupe on application side.
[03:12] Daniel Cho: how long is the idempotency window?
[03:15] Maya Singh: default 60 seconds; can be configured for POCs on Dedicated.
[03:20] Alex Park: and if you need exactly-once semantics for billing you can route through Dedicated with sticky sessions.

[03:28] Priya Raman: what about parameters \u2014 temp, top_p, max_tokens \u2014 any Redwood-specific defaults?
[03:33] Maya Singh: defaults align with common open models: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95. you can override per-request. also we support stop sequences, frequency_penalty, and logit_bias. here's a quick show: lower temp reduces creativity, ideal for assistant style answers.
[03:50] [03:52] Daniel Cho: do you support function/tool-calling?
[03:55] Maya Singh: yes, for supported models there is structured output and tool calling. demo will not show full tools, but it's supported in hosted API.

[04:05] Alex Park: let's talk throughput \u2014 if you have bursty traffic patterns, hosted can autoscale but you may hit cold-start or throttling. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p99.
[04:18] Daniel Cho: our workload is bursty during business hours with spikes up to 400 rps for short periods. cost sensitivity is high.
[04:27] Alex Park: for that profile we usually recommend a hybrid approach: Hosted for dev + low-traffic routes, Dedicated reservation for high-throughput critical routes. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching & quantization profiles to reduce cost.

[04:42] [04:45] Priya Raman: what's the request/response size limit?
[04:48] Maya Singh: message payloads up to 8k tokens for certain models; depends on model. we'll share model catalog with max context length per model.

[05:00] Maya Singh: moving back to streaming internals \u2014 we emit chunk events roughly every N tokens; client SDKs present them as delta updates. there are two common integration patterns: 1) append-as-you-go for UX, 2) optimistic rendering where you show typing indicator until threshold. both supported.
[05:20] [05:22] Speaker 2: right

[05:25] Daniel Cho: can you talk about pricing impact of streaming? you said tokens billing still applies, but are there per-request costs?
[05:31] Alex Park: no per-stream surcharge; billing is token-based plus any region egress. we also provide cost breakdowns in console per-route and per-token-type (input vs output).

[05:45] Maya Singh: demoing retries: here's a sample response showing a partial content delta and then an error frame. show code snippet where client does exponential backoff and uses same request_id.
[05:59] Priya Raman: if a client reconnects and resumes, does Redwood replay only remaining tokens or full?
[06:06] Maya Singh: we attempt to replay from last known checkpoint if we have KV cache and partial result recorded; otherwise we regenerate. this can lead to minor differences in tokens \u2014 so for deterministic output use model selection + smaller temperature.

[06:20] Daniel Cho: you mentioned KV cache \u2014 is that per-customer?
[06:23] Maya Singh: yes, KV cache is per-session/per-model instance, and we have TTLs. for Hosted it's managed; on Dedicated you have more control over eviction and cache sizing.

[06:34] [06:36] Alex Park: security \u2014 data at rest encrypted, you can bring your own KMS for Private/Dedicated. retention policies can be set per-account.

[06:46] Daniel Cho: HIPAA-ish requirements \u2014 how do you handle PHI?
[06:50] Maya Singh: we offer Private deployment and contractual terms for regulated workloads; Hosted can be used with careful data filters and short retention but for true PHI workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer managed keys.

[07:02] Priya Raman: are logs and audit trails accessible?
[07:05] Maya Singh: yes, console exposes request-level logs, latency, token counts, and exportable audit logs.

[07:12] Alex Park: quick aside on model variants \u2014 we surface smaller, quantized variants for cost-sensitive workloads with some perf/quality tradeoff. Optimize tool can suggest quantization per workload.

[07:28] [07:30] Daniel Cho: can we bring our weights or custom finetunes?
[07:33] Maya Singh: we support customer models via Private deployment and private model hosting on Dedicated. Hosted gives curated open models and vendor models we verify. For full custom models you would look at Private or a Dedicated bring-your-own option.

[07:48] Priya Raman: what's the rollout for model updates? we need version pinning and canary tests.
[07:52] Alex Park: you can pin model versions per route and do canary rollouts with automatic fallback. Console shows per-model metrics and you can wire automated rollback based on evals.

[08:05] [08:10] Maya Singh: showing the console \u2014 route config page: per-route model, max tokens, timeout, and retry policy. you can set retries 0-3 with backoff and idempotency settings.

[08:22] Daniel Cho: how do you measure quality regressions?

[08:25] Maya Singh: Redwood has an evals integration where we run prompt sets and compute regressions, tie alerts to rollouts. we'll share an example report.

[08:36] Priya Raman: latency SLOs \u2014 what can you promise on Hosted vs Dedicated?

[08:40] Alex Park: Hosted is best-effort with region-aware routing; Dedicated has SLA-backed latency/uptime. typical p95 on Dedicated for our small LMs is under 200ms depending on config.

[08:52] [09:00] Daniel Cho: can you run a quick cost estimate? say 2M tokens/month with 60% output tokens and a mix of small plus medium models.

[09:08] Alex Park: sure \u2014 rough back-of-envelope: cost per 1k tokens depends on model; we'll send a detailed pricing sheet, but Optimize can run simulation with your token distribution and recommend quantized variant to reduce spend.

[09:25] Priya Raman: are there sample SDKs for streaming reconnections?

[09:28] Maya Singh: yes \u2014 JS and Python SDKs with reconnect helpers and idempotency keys; we also provide streaming SSE and WebSocket examples.

[09:40] [09:45] Alex Park: wrapping up demo \u2014 main takeaways: streaming reduces perceived latency, use idempotency keys for safe retries, Dedicated if you need predictable throughput/SLA, and Optimize can reduce cost.

[09:58] Daniel Cho: this was useful. a few follow-ups: can you share SOC2, details on KMS integration, and price sheet? also we want to run a POC with our prompt set.

[10:10] Alex Park: absolutely. next steps: I'll send pricing + Dedicated quote; Maya will share security pack and model catalog; we'll schedule POC benchmarking \u2014 suggested week of 3/11.

[10:20] Priya Raman: timeline wise we want a decision in 3-4 weeks if POC looks good, and are concerned about ramping costs.

[10:28] Alex Park: understood \u2014 Optimize will be helpful; we'll include a cost projection.

[10:34] Maya Singh: any other technical Qs?

[10:36] Daniel Cho: one last: how do you handle partial token billing when a stream is dropped mid-response?

[10:40] Maya Singh: you are billed for tokens generated server-side. if generation completed but client didn't receive due to network, tokens still billed. idempotency/resume helps avoid duplicate full-generation. we'll discuss guardrails in the POC.

[10:52] Alex Park: ok great \u2014 we'll follow up with the docs and pricing. thanks everyone for your time.

[10:58] Priya Raman: thanks, this helped.

[11:00] Daniel Cho: thanks Alex, Maya. bye.

--- End meeting transcript ---
